derivations.claim: For an interior face $F=K|L$, the shared-flux definitions give $Q_{K,F}(u)+Q_{L,F}(u)=T_F(u_K-u_L)+T_F(u_L-u_K)=0$. Thus summing cell balances cancels every interior flux exactly.

In $\sum_K |K|v_K(A_hu)_K$, the two terms contributed by an interior face are $T_F[v_K(u_K-u_L)+v_L(u_L-u_K)]=T_F(v_K-v_L)(u_K-u_L)$. A boundary face contributes $T_{K,F}v_Ku_K$. Summing all faces proves the displayed identity.

Set $v=u$ in step 1.2. The resulting stiffness quadratic form is a sum of nonnegative terms. If it is zero, every interior term forces $u_K=u_L$, and every boundary term forces $u_K=0$ on its incident cell. The path condition [A1] propagates these zeros through the connected cell graph, so $u=0$. The finite-dimensional symmetric stiffness matrix therefore has trivial kernel and is positive definite and invertible. Since the volume matrix $M_h=\operatorname{diag}(|K|)$ is invertible, $A_h=M_h^{-1}(M_hA_h)$ is also invertible; inhomogeneous boundary values change only the right-hand side.

Suppose $u$ solves the cell balances with $f_K\ge0$ and $g_F\ge0$. If a cell value has a negative global minimum, choose a minimizing cell $K$. Every interior summand $T_F(u_K-u_L)$ in its balance is nonpositive, and every boundary summand $T_{K,F}(u_K-g_F)$ is strictly negative. Since the balance equals $|K|f_K\ge0$, all summands must be zero. Thus the minimum propagates unchanged to every adjacent cell along a path from [A1], but at a boundary face the summand $T_{K,F}(u_K-g_F)$ is strictly negative. This contradiction rules out a negative minimum, so all cell values are nonnegative.

derivations.claim: Fix a cell $K$. Traverse its supplied path to a boundary face. The signed increments telescope from $u_K$ to the terminal boundary value $0$, so $u_K=\sum_{e\in\gamma_K}\epsilon_{K,e}\Delta_eu$, where each $\epsilon_{K,e}\in\{-1,1\}$ records the orientation.
Weighted Cauchy–Schwarz with weights $T_e$ gives $|u_K|^2\le(\sum_{e\in\gamma_K}T_e^{-1})(\sum_{e\in\gamma_K}T_e(\Delta_eu)^2)=S_K\sum_{e\in\gamma_K}T_e(\Delta_eu)^2$.

Multiply step 2.1 by $|K|$ and sum over all cells. Since the mesh, edge set, and paths are finite, reorder the sums to obtain $\sum_K|K|u_K^2\le\sum_eT_e(\Delta_eu)^2\sum_{K:e\in\gamma_K}|K|S_K\le C_{\rm path}\sum_eT_e(\Delta_eu)^2.$ The last sum is the energy norm in [F2], proving the assertion.

Let $\mathcal T$ be a cell-face mesh as in [[def-fv-admissible-cell-face-mesh]], with $x_K$ the volume centroid of each cell and $x_F$ the face centroid. For the mimetic branch require the following explicit face-moment closure on each cell:
$$ \sum_{F\subset\partial K}|F|n_{K,F}=0,\qquad \sum_{F\subset\partial K}|F|x_F\otimes n_{K,F}=|K|I_d. $$
Here $I_d$ is the identity matrix on $\mathbb R^d$ and $(x\otimes n)_{ij}=x_i n_j$. These are finite geometric checks on the face data; they impose no center-to-face orthogonality. For every cell use one real cell-mean unknown $u_K$; for every face use one shared real face-mean unknown $u_F$. On a boundary face $F\subset\partial\Omega$, the value $u_F=g_F$ is prescribed. Write $n_{K,F}$ for the outward unit normal. Define the reconstructed cell gradient and its face residual by
$$ G_Ku=\frac1{|K|}\sum_{F\subset\partial K}|F|u_Fn_{K,F},\qquad \rho_{K,F}(u)=u_F-u_K-G_Ku\cdot(x_F-x_K). $$
Interpret $u_K$ and $u_F$ as cell and face averages. For a symmetric positive-definite tensor $A_K$ constant on $K$ (so $z\cdot A_Kz>0$ for every nonzero $z$), define
$$ \mathscr A_K(u,v)=|K|(A_KG_Ku)\cdot G_Kv+\lambda_{\min}(A_K)\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\frac{|F|}{d_{K,F}}\rho_{K,F}(u)\rho_{K,F}(v), $$
where $\lambda_{\min}(A_K)>0$ is the smallest eigenvalue of $A_K$. The **linear hybrid mimetic scheme** with homogeneous Dirichlet data is to find all cell and interior-face values $u$ such that
$$ \sum_{K\in\mathcal K}\mathscr A_K(u,v)=\sum_{K\in\mathcal K}v_K\int_K f(x)\,dx $$
for every test vector $v$ whose boundary face values are zero. For each local face $F\subset\partial K$, let $\phi_{K,F}$ have face value $1$ on $F$, zero on the other faces of $K$, and cell value zero. Define the outward numerical flux $Q_{K,F}(u)=-\mathscr A_K(u,\phi_{K,F})$.

There is also a monotone $p$-growth backward-Euler extension, specified as an algebraic scheme but with no existence or convergence claim in this definition. Let $1<p<\infty$, set $p'=p/(p-1)$, and let $a(x,\xi)$ be a **Carathéodory flux**, meaning that $x\mapsto a(x,\xi)$ is measurable for each fixed $\xi$ and $\xi\mapsto a(x,\xi)$ is continuous for almost every $x$. Assume there are constants $C,\alpha>0$, a nonnegative $g\in L^{p'}(\Omega)$, and a nonnegative $h\in L^1(\Omega)$ such that, outside one null set,
$$ |a(x,\xi)|\le C(g(x)+|\xi|^{p-1}),\qquad a(x,\xi)\cdot\xi\ge\alpha|\xi|^p-h(x),\qquad (a(x,\xi)-a(x,\eta))\cdot(\xi-\eta)\ge0. $$
For each cell set $b_K(\xi)=|K|^{-1}\int_Ka(x,\xi)\,dx$, and fix $\alpha_{0,K}>0$. Put $\psi_p(s)=|s|^{p-2}s$ for $s\ne0$ and $\psi_p(0)=0$. Its spatial operator, linear in the test vector $v$, is
$$ \mathcal A_{h,K}(u;v)=|K|b_K(G_Ku)\cdot G_Kv+\alpha_{0,K}\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\frac{|F|}{d_{K,F}^{p-1}}\psi_p(\rho_{K,F}(u))\rho_{K,F}(v). $$
For this extension define $Q_{K,F}^{\rm nl}(u)=-\mathcal A_{h,K}(u;\phi_{K,F})$.
On a time partition $0=t_0<\cdots<t_N=T$, given $u^{n-1}$ and $f\in L^{p'}((0,T)\times\Omega)$, put $f_K^n=((t_n-t_{n-1})|K|)^{-1}\int_{t_{n-1}}^{t_n}\int_K f$. The backward-Euler step seeks $u^n$ with zero boundary face values satisfying
$$ \sum_{K\in\mathcal K}|K|\frac{u_K^n-u_K^{n-1}}{t_n-t_{n-1}}v_K+\sum_{K\in\mathcal K}\mathcal A_{h,K}(u^n;v)=\sum_{K\in\mathcal K}|K|f_K^n v_K $$
for every test vector with zero boundary face values. The formula specifies a candidate discrete method; solvability and convergence require separate results.

For an affine function $\ell(x)=b\cdot x+c$, its cell and face averages satisfy $G_K\ell=b$ and $\rho_{K,F}(\ell)=0$ by the displayed face-moment closure. The drawing illustrates the cell and face degrees of freedom on a skew cell; no center-to-face orthogonality is assumed.

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=1]
  \draw[thick] (0,0) -- (2,0) -- (3,1) -- (1,1) -- cycle;
  \fill (1.5,0.5) circle (2pt) node[below] {$u_K$};
  \fill (1,0) circle (2pt) node[below] {$u_{F_1}$};
  \fill (2.5,0.5) circle (2pt) node[right] {$u_{F_2}$};
  \fill (2,1) circle (2pt) node[above] {$u_{F_3}$};
  \fill (0.5,0.5) circle (2pt) node[left] {$u_{F_4}$};
  \draw[->,blue] (1.5,0.5) -- (2.2,0.5) node[right] {$G_Ku$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

When $p=2$, $b_K(\xi)=A_K\xi$, and $\alpha_{0,K}=\lambda_{\min}(A_K)$, the nonlinear formula agrees with the linear form above. Neither specification by itself proves solvability, a conforming $W_0^{1,p}$ reconstruction, or a mesh-uniform discrete Aubin–Lions estimate; those require separate results or hypotheses.

derivations.claim: For an affine $\ell(x)=b\cdot x+c$, the cell and face means are $\ell_K=\ell(x_K)$ and $\ell_F=\ell(x_F)$. The first face-moment identity annihilates the constant term in $G_K\ell$; the transpose of the second identity is $\sum_F|F|n_{K,F}\otimes x_F=|K|I_d$, so $G_K\ell=b$. Hence $\rho_{K,F}(\ell)=\ell_F-\ell_K-b\cdot(x_F-x_K)=0$.

For arbitrary $v$, [A1] gives $|K|(A_KG_Kv)\cdot G_Kv\ge\lambda_{\min}(A_K)|K||G_Kv|^2$. The stabilization coefficient is $\lambda_{\min}(A_K)>0$, so summing its squared residual terms gives $\mathscr A_K(v,v)\ge\lambda_{\min}(A_K)\|v\|_{K,\mathrm{mim}}^2$.

For the nonlinear flux, the cell average preserves monotonicity because $(b_K(\xi)-b_K(\eta))\cdot(\xi-\eta)=\frac1{|K|}\int_K(a(x,\xi)-a(x,\eta))\cdot(\xi-\eta)\,dx\ge0.$ The pointwise bounds in [A2] also give $b_K(\xi)\cdot\xi\ge\alpha|\xi|^p-|K|^{-1}\int_Kh$ and $|b_K(\xi)|\le C(|K|^{-1}\int_Kg+|\xi|^{p-1})$. Thus the averaged flux retains monotonicity, coercivity, and $p$-growth.

The global form is symmetric because each $A_K$ is symmetric and the residual term is a symmetric product. If its energy at $v$ is zero, step 1.2 forces $G_Kv=0$ and every $\rho_{K,F}(v)=0$. The latter then gives $v_F=v_K$ on every face. Shared face values make all adjacent cell values equal, and a boundary face has prescribed value zero; boundary anchoring propagates this zero to every cell. Thus the homogeneous matrix has trivial kernel. It is square and finite-dimensional, so it is invertible and positive definite; every cell-source vector has a unique solution.

For an interior face $F=K|L$, the global equation tested by its shared face basis function gives $\mathscr A_K(u,\phi_{K,F})+\mathscr A_L(u,\phi_{L,F})=0$, hence $Q_{K,F}+Q_{L,F}=0$. For a cell basis $\phi_K$, the equation gives $\mathscr A_K(u,\phi_K)=\int_Kf$. The local constant vector $\mathbf1_K=\phi_K+\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\phi_{K,F}$ has zero reconstructed gradient by the first face-moment identity and zero residual; therefore $\mathscr A_K(u,\mathbf1_K)=0$. Expanding this identity and using the cell equation yields $\sum_{F\subset\partial K}Q_{K,F}=\int_Kf$.

If $u$ is the face and cell averages of an affine $\ell$, step 1.1 gives $G_Ku=b$ and all residuals of $u$ vanish. For the local face basis, $G_K\phi_{K,F}=|F|n_{K,F}/|K|$. Thus $\mathscr A_K(u,\phi_{K,F})=|F|(A_Kb)\cdot n_{K,F}$, and the definition $Q_{K,F}=-\mathscr A_K(u,\phi_{K,F})$ gives the exact outward diffusive flux.

The scalar map $\psi_p(s)=|s|^{p-2}s$ is increasing: it is increasing on each half-line by monotonicity of $r\mapsto r^{p-1}$ for $r\ge0$, and its values are nonpositive on $s\le0$ and nonnegative on $s\ge0$. Hence $(\psi_p(r)-\psi_p(s))(r-s)\ge0$. For any two states $u,v$, the difference $\mathcal A_{h,K}(u;u-v)-\mathcal A_{h,K}(v;u-v)$ is the sum of $|K|(b_K(G_Ku)-b_K(G_Kv))\cdot(G_Ku-G_Kv)$ and the nonnegative residual terms $\alpha_{0,K}|F|d_{K,F}^{1-p}(\psi_p(\rho_{K,F}(u))-\psi_p(\rho_{K,F}(v)))(\rho_{K,F}(u)-\rho_{K,F}(v))$. Step 1.3 and scalar monotonicity make every term nonnegative. Testing with $v=u$ and using the coercivity bound in [A2] yields $\mathcal A_{h,K}(u;u)\ge |K|\left(\alpha|G_Ku|^p-|K|^{-1}\int_Kh\right)+\alpha_{0,K}\sum_F\frac{|F|}{d_{K,F}^{p-1}}|\rho_{K,F}(u)|^p.$ For a fixed state, the local constant test vector has zero gradient and residual, so the spatial form annihilates it. A shared interior-face test in an implicit step makes $Q_{K,F}^{\rm nl}+Q_{L,F}^{\rm nl}=0$. Testing the step equation by the cell basis gives $\mathcal A_{h,K}(u^n;\phi_K)=|K|f_K^n-|K|(u_K^n-u_K^{n-1})/\tau_n$. Expanding the zero constant-test identity gives $\sum_FQ_{K,F}^{\rm nl}=|K|f_K^n-|K|(u_K^n-u_K^{n-1})/\tau_n$, the local balance with accumulation.

citations.quote:
Let $\mathcal T$ be a finite TPFA-admissible cell-face mesh, let every cell be connected through interior faces to a cell with a boundary face, and let $T_F>0$ be the transmissibilities of [[def-tpfa-harmonic-face-scheme]]. For cell vectors $u,v$, define
$$ (A_hu)_K=\frac1{|K|}\left(\sum_{F=K|L}T_F(u_K-u_L)+\sum_{F\subset\partial K\cap\partial\Omega}T_{K,F}u_K\right). $$
Then interior fluxes are locally conservative, and for all cell vectors $u,v$,
$$ \sum_{K\in\mathcal K}|K|v_K(A_hu)_K= \sum_{F=K|L\in\mathcal F_{\rm int}}T_F(v_K-v_L)(u_K-u_L) +\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_{\rm bdy}}T_{K,F}v_Ku_K. $$
The stiffness matrix associated with the displayed bilinear identity is symmetric positive definite. Equivalently, $A_h$ is self-adjoint and positive definite in the volume-weighted inner product $\langle u,v\rangle_h=\sum_K|K|u_Kv_K$; its ordinary coordinate matrix need not be symmetric when cell volumes differ. Hence every finite source and boundary-data vector gives a unique solution. If all cell sources and all prescribed boundary face values are nonnegative, then every solution cell value is nonnegative. The maximum-principle claim uses the boundary anchor; no diagonal sign statement alone is used as a substitute for that condition.

derivations.claim: For each face orient the exact flux $J_F$ outward from one incident cell, and set $\delta_F=Q_{K,F}(I_hu)-J_F$; on a boundary face set $\delta_F=Q_{K,F}(I_hu)-J_{K,F}$. Let $y_F$ be the intersection of the center-normal line with an interior face and the orthogonal projection point on a boundary face. Taylor's theorem along the normal gives, on $F=K|L$ with $n=n_{K,F}$, $u(x_K)=u(y_F)-d_{K,F}\partial_nu_K(y_F)+r_K,\quad u(x_L)=u(y_F)+d_{L,F}\partial_nu_L(y_F)+r_L,$ where $|r_K|+|r_L|\le C M h^2$. By [A1], $\lambda_K\partial_nu_K(y_F)=\lambda_L\partial_nu_L(y_F)=s_F$. Substitution into the harmonic formula gives $Q_{K,F}(I_hu)=-|F|s_F+T_F(r_K-r_L)$. The face trace varies by at most $M h$ from $y_F$, so $|J_{K,F}+|F|s_F|\le C\lambda^*M|F|h$. Since [F1]–[F2] imply $T_F\le C|F|/h$, we obtain $|\delta_F|\le C M|F|h$. On a boundary face, $u(y_F)=0$ and the one-sided Taylor expansion $u(x_K)=-d_{K,F}\partial_nu_K(y_F)+r_K$ yields the same bound for $\delta_F$.

By uniform regularity, every transmissibility satisfies $T_F\ge c|F|/h$. There are at most $N_0$ faces per cell, $|F|\le Ch^{d-1}$, and $|K|\ge ch^d$, so $\#\mathcal K_h\le |\Omega|/(ch^d)$ and $\sum_F|F|\le C h^{-1}$. Step 1.1 therefore gives $\sum_F\frac{\delta_F^2}{T_F}\le C M^2h^3\sum_F|F|\le C M^2h^2.$ Thus the vector of local flux defects has transmissibility-dual norm at most $C hM$.

Let $e=U_h-I_hu$. The exact cell balances in [A1] and the finite-volume balances for $U_h$ imply, for every cell vector $v$, $a_h(e,v)=-\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_{\rm int}}\delta_F(v_K-v_L)-\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_{\rm bdy}}\delta_Fv_K,$ because the two exact interior fluxes are oppositely oriented. Take $v=e$. Weighted Cauchy–Schwarz gives $\|e\|_{E_h}^2\le(\sum_F\delta_F^2/T_F)^{1/2}\|e\|_{E_h}$. If $e=0$ the first estimate is immediate; otherwise divide by $\|e\|_{E_h}$ and use step 2.1 to obtain $\|e\|_{E_h}\le ChM$. The bilinear identity used here is [F3].

On every face, $Q_{K,F}(U_h)-Q_{K,F}(I_hu)$ equals $T_F(e_K-e_L)$ for an interior face and $T_{K,F}e_K$ for a boundary face. Its transmissibility-dual norm is therefore exactly $\|e\|_{E_h}$. By the triangle inequality, the numerical-flux error norm is at most $\|e\|_{E_h}+(\sum_F\delta_F^2/T_F)^{1/2}\le2ChM$, using steps 2.1 and 3.1. This proves both estimates.

Let $V$ be a separable reflexive real Banach space, let $H$ be a real Hilbert
space, and let $i:V\to H$ be an injective continuous linear map with dense
range. Let $V^*$ be the continuous real dual of $V$ and write
$\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_{V^*,V}$ for its pairing with $V$. The canonical
map $J:H\to V^*$ is
$$J h(v)=(h,iv)_H\qquad(h\in H,\ v\in V).$$
It is continuous because $|Jh(v)|\le \|h\|_H\|i\|\|v\|_V$, and injective
because $i(V)$ is dense in $H$. A triple $(V,H,J)$ with these properties is
a **Banach evolution triple**. If $V$ is Hilbert, this is the real evolution
triple of [[def-parabolic-evolution-triple-and-energy-space]].

For $1<p<\infty$, $L^p(0,T;V)$ denotes the Bochner space of strongly
measurable $V$-valued functions with finite $p$th power norm, and
$p'=p/(p-1)$. For $u\in L^p(0,T;V)$ and $g\in L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)$, say
$g=u'$ in the distributional time sense if
$$\int_0^T (iu(t),iv)_H\,\phi'(t)\,dt =-\int_0^T\langle g(t),v\rangle_{V^*,V}\,\phi(t)\,dt$$
for every $v\in V$ and $\phi\in C_c^\infty(0,T)$. Define
$$W_p(0,T;V)=\{u\in L^p(0,T;V):u'\in L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)\}.$$
This definition assigns no endpoint values; a separate chain-rule theorem is
needed before evaluating a function in this space at an endpoint.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

Let $d\ge1$, let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded open set, and
let $1<p<\infty$ satisfy $p>\max(1,2d/(d+2))$. Put
$V=W_0^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ with norm
$\|v\|_V=\|\nabla v\|_{L^p(\Omega)}$, $H=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$, and
$p'=p/(p-1)$. The Poincaré inequality makes this norm equivalent to the full
$W^{1,p}$ norm. [[lem-pe12-w0p-separable-reflexive]] gives separability and
reflexivity, while [[lem-pe12-w1p-compact-l2-embedding]] gives the dense
continuous compact inclusion $V\Subset H$; these are the hypotheses of the
evolution triple in [[def-pe12-gelfand-triple]]. The compact-inclusion result
uses the stated threshold also when $d=1$, where it reduces to $p>1$.

A measurable flux $a:\Omega\times\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$ is an admissible
**coercive monotone diffusion flux of p-growth** if it is Carathéodory (for
each $\xi$, $x\mapsto a(x,\xi)$ is measurable, and for almost every $x$,
$\xi\mapsto a(x,\xi)$ is continuous), and there are constants $C<\infty$,
$\alpha>0$, nonnegative functions $g\in L^{p'}(\Omega)$ and
$h\in L^1(\Omega)$, and one
null set outside which, for all $\xi,\eta\in\mathbb R^d$,
$$|a(x,\xi)|\le C\bigl(g(x)+|\xi|^{p-1}\bigr),\qquad a(x,\xi)\cdot\xi\ge\alpha|\xi|^p-h(x),$$
$$\bigl(a(x,\xi)-a(x,\eta)\bigr)\cdot(\xi-\eta)\ge0.$$
The induced operator $A:V\to V^*$ is
$$\langle A(v),w\rangle_{V^*,V} =\int_\Omega a(x,\nabla v(x))\cdot\nabla w(x)\,dx.$$
The growth bound and Hölder's inequality make this pairing finite and give
$\|A(v)\|_{V^*}\le C_1(\|g\|_{p'}+\|v\|_V^{p-1})$ for a constant $C_1$.
For the finite-dimensional existence result below we additionally require
that this induced map $A:V\to V^*$ is norm-continuous; this is verified
directly for the p-Laplacian in the companion example.

For $f\in L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)$, a weak evolution solution is a function
$u\in W_p(0,T;V)\cap L^\infty(0,T;H)$ with a continuous $H$ representative
such that $u'+A(u)=f$ in $L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)$ and $u(0)=u_0\in H$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let
$\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be bounded and open, $d\ge1$, let
$1<p<\infty$, and let $0<T<\infty$. Put $V=W_0^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ with gradient norm
$\|v\|_V=\|\nabla v\|_{L^p}$, and suppose $V$ has a continuous inclusion in
a real Hilbert space $H$. If $u_j$ is bounded in $L^p(0,T;V)$ and its image
in $L^p(0,T;H)$ converges strongly to $u$, then a subsequence converges
weakly in $L^p(0,T;V)$ to some $U$, the image of $U$ equals $u$, and
$\nabla u_j\rightharpoonup\nabla U$ in
$L^p((0,T)\times\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice.

Let $Q=(0,T)\times\Omega$ have finite measure, $1<p<\infty$, and let
$a(x,\xi)$ be a Carathéodory flux with the monotonicity and $p$-growth
hypotheses of [[def-pe12-monotone-diffusion-flux]], independent of time.
Suppose $\xi_n\rightharpoonup\xi$ in $L^p(Q;\mathbb R^d)$,
$q_n=a(x,\xi_n)\rightharpoonup q$ in $L^{p'}(Q;\mathbb R^d)$, and
$$\limsup_{n\to\infty}\int_Q q_n\cdot\xi_n \le\int_Qq\cdot\xi.$$
Then $q(x,t)=a(x,\xi(x,t))$ for almost every $(t,x)\in Q$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let
$(V,H,J)$ be the Banach evolution triple of
[[def-pe12-gelfand-triple]], let $1<p<\infty$, and suppose
$u\in L^p(0,T;V)\cap L^\infty(0,T;H)$ with distributional derivative
$u'\in L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)$. Then $u$ has a unique representative in
$C([0,T];H)$ and, for every $0\le s\le t\le T$,
$$\|u(t)\|_H^2-\|u(s)\|_H^2 =2\int_s^t\langle u'(r),u(r)\rangle_{V^*,V}\,dr.$$

Assume the Axiom of Choice for the ACL and absolutely-continuous
fundamental-theorem interfaces. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open
interval, let $1\le p\le\infty$, let $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$,
and let $u\in W^{1,p}(I;\mathbb K)$, with weak derivative class $Du$. Then
there is exactly one continuous representative $u^*$ of the class of $u$ on
$I$ that is locally absolutely continuous, that is, absolutely continuous on
every compact interval contained in $I$, and satisfies
$$u^*(x)-u^*(y)=\int_y^xDu(t)\,dt\qquad\text{for every }x,y\in I,$$
where for $x<y$ the right-hand side denotes $-\int_x^yDu$, equivalently
$u^*(y)-u^*(x)=\int_x^yDu$ whenever $x\le y$.

If $I=(a,b)$ has finite endpoints, then $Du\in L^1(a,b)$, the representative
$u^*$ extends uniquely to an absolutely continuous function on $[a,b]$, and
the extension satisfies
$$u^*(x)=u^*(a)+\int_a^xDu(t)\,dt\qquad\text{for every }x\in[a,b].$$

The scalar field is arbitrary, $p=1$ and $p=\infty$ are included, and the
one-dimensional interval may be bounded or unbounded. The Axiom of Choice is
used only through the Countable-Choice and Dependent-Choice hypotheses of the
cited characterisation, fundamental-theorem and completeness interfaces.

derivations.claim: The strong convergence $\bar U_m\to u$ and the reconstruction estimate in [A2] imply $w_m\to u$ strongly in $L^p(0,T;H)$. The sequence is bounded in $L^p(0,T;V)$, so [F3] gives, after subsequence extraction, $w_m\rightharpoonup u$ in $L^p(0,T;V)$ and $\xi_m=\nabla w_m\rightharpoonup\nabla u$ in $L^p(Q;\mathbb R^d)$.

Fix $\varphi\in C_c^\infty([0,T)	imes\Omega)$. Strong convergence of $ ar U_m$ gives $\int_Q ar U_m\partial_t\varphi	o\int_Qu\partial_t\varphi$; weak convergence of $q_m$ gives $\int_Qq_m\cdot
abla\varphi	o\int_Qq\cdot
abla\varphi$. The source and initial terms are fixed, and [A2] gives $r_m(\varphi)	o0$. Passing to the limit in the discrete weak identity therefore yields $-\int_Qu\,\partial_t\varphi+\int_Qq\cdot
abla\varphi=\int_Qf\varphi+\int_\Omega u_0\varphi(\cdot,0).$

Step 1.1 gives $\xi_m\rightharpoonup\nabla u$ in $L^p$, the statement gives $q_m=a(x,\xi_m)\rightharpoonup q$ in $L^{p'}$, and the assumed energy limsup is exactly the remaining hypothesis of [F4]. Thus [F4] implies $q=a(x,\nabla u)$ almost everywhere.

For $v\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ and $\theta\in C_c^\infty(0,T)$, use $\varphi(t,x)=\theta(t)v(x)$ in step 2.1. The weak identity shows in distributions that $u'=g$, where $\langle g(t),v\rangle=\int_\Omega f(t,x)v(x)\,dx-\int_\Omega q(t,x)\cdot\nabla v(x)\,dx$. By H\"older and the Poincar\'e norm equivalence in [F2], $\|g(t)\|_{V^*}\le C_P\|f(t)\|_{L^{p'}(\Omega)}+\|q(t)\|_{L^{p'}(\Omega)}$ for almost every $t$. Thus $g\in L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)$. The identity extends from smooth $v$ to every $v\in V$ by the defining density of $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ in $W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$ and the displayed bound, so it is the distributional derivative from [F1]. Hence $u\in W_p(0,T;V)$.
By [A1], [A3], step 3.1, and the assumed $u\in L^p(0,T;V)$, the continuous-trace theorem [F5] gives a unique representative $u\in C([0,T];H)$.

Fix $v\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ and $\theta\in C_c^\infty([0,T))$. The scalar function $t\mapsto(u(t),v)_H$ is bounded on $(0,T)$ by [A3], and its distributional derivative $t\mapsto\langle u'(t),v\rangle$ lies in $L^1(0,T)$ by step 3.1 and finite $T$. Thus it belongs to $W^{1,1}(0,T)$, so [A1] and [F6] give an absolutely continuous representative and integration by parts on $[0,T]$. This representative agrees almost everywhere with the continuous scalar function from step 4.1; since both are continuous, they agree everywhere, including at $t=0$. Apply step 2.1 to $\varphi=\theta v$ and use $\langle u',v\rangle=\int fv-\int q\cdot\nabla v$ from step 3.1. The bulk terms cancel and leave $(u(0)-u_0,v)_H\theta(0)=0$. Choose $\theta(0)=1$. This holds for every smooth compactly supported $v$, which is dense in $H$; therefore $u(0)=u_0$ in $H$.

By step 3.1 and the definition of the induced operator in [F2], $u'+A(u)=f$ in $L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)$ after substituting $q=a(x,\nabla u)$ from step 2.2. Step 4.1 gives the required continuous $H$ representative and step 5.1 gives its initial trace. These are exactly the weak evolution solution conditions of [F2].

Let $\mathcal T$ be a cell-face mesh as in [[def-fv-admissible-cell-face-mesh]], with $x_K$ the volume centroid of each cell and $x_F$ the face centroid. For the mimetic branch require the following explicit face-moment closure on each cell:
$$ \sum_{F\subset\partial K}|F|n_{K,F}=0,\qquad \sum_{F\subset\partial K}|F|x_F\otimes n_{K,F}=|K|I_d. $$
Here $I_d$ is the identity matrix on $\mathbb R^d$ and $(x\otimes n)_{ij}=x_i n_j$. These are finite geometric checks on the face data; they impose no center-to-face orthogonality. For every cell use one real cell-mean unknown $u_K$; for every face use one shared real face-mean unknown $u_F$. On a boundary face $F\subset\partial\Omega$, the value $u_F=g_F$ is prescribed. Write $n_{K,F}$ for the outward unit normal. Define the reconstructed cell gradient and its face residual by
$$ G_Ku=\frac1{|K|}\sum_{F\subset\partial K}|F|u_Fn_{K,F},\qquad \rho_{K,F}(u)=u_F-u_K-G_Ku\cdot(x_F-x_K). $$
Interpret $u_K$ and $u_F$ as cell and face averages. For a symmetric positive-definite tensor $A_K$ constant on $K$ (so $z\cdot A_Kz>0$ for every nonzero $z$), define
$$ \mathscr A_K(u,v)=|K|(A_KG_Ku)\cdot G_Kv+\lambda_{\min}(A_K)\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\frac{|F|}{d_{K,F}}\rho_{K,F}(u)\rho_{K,F}(v), $$
where $\lambda_{\min}(A_K)>0$ is the smallest eigenvalue of $A_K$. The **linear hybrid mimetic scheme** with homogeneous Dirichlet data is to find all cell and interior-face values $u$ such that
$$ \sum_{K\in\mathcal K}\mathscr A_K(u,v)=\sum_{K\in\mathcal K}v_K\int_K f(x)\,dx $$
for every test vector $v$ whose boundary face values are zero. For each local face $F\subset\partial K$, let $\phi_{K,F}$ have face value $1$ on $F$, zero on the other faces of $K$, and cell value zero. Define the outward numerical flux $Q_{K,F}(u)=-\mathscr A_K(u,\phi_{K,F})$.

There is also a monotone $p$-growth backward-Euler extension, specified as an algebraic scheme but with no existence or convergence claim in this definition. Let $1<p<\infty$, set $p'=p/(p-1)$, and let $a(x,\xi)$ be a **Carathéodory flux**, meaning that $x\mapsto a(x,\xi)$ is measurable for each fixed $\xi$ and $\xi\mapsto a(x,\xi)$ is continuous for almost every $x$. Assume there are constants $C,\alpha>0$, a nonnegative $g\in L^{p'}(\Omega)$, and a nonnegative $h\in L^1(\Omega)$ such that, outside one null set,
$$ |a(x,\xi)|\le C(g(x)+|\xi|^{p-1}),\qquad a(x,\xi)\cdot\xi\ge\alpha|\xi|^p-h(x),\qquad (a(x,\xi)-a(x,\eta))\cdot(\xi-\eta)\ge0. $$
For each cell set $b_K(\xi)=|K|^{-1}\int_Ka(x,\xi)\,dx$, and fix $\alpha_{0,K}>0$. Put $\psi_p(s)=|s|^{p-2}s$ for $s\ne0$ and $\psi_p(0)=0$. Its spatial operator, linear in the test vector $v$, is
$$ \mathcal A_{h,K}(u;v)=|K|b_K(G_Ku)\cdot G_Kv+\alpha_{0,K}\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\frac{|F|}{d_{K,F}^{p-1}}\psi_p(\rho_{K,F}(u))\rho_{K,F}(v). $$
For this extension define $Q_{K,F}^{\rm nl}(u)=-\mathcal A_{h,K}(u;\phi_{K,F})$.
On a time partition $0=t_0<\cdots<t_N=T$, given $u^{n-1}$ and $f\in L^{p'}((0,T)\times\Omega)$, put $f_K^n=((t_n-t_{n-1})|K|)^{-1}\int_{t_{n-1}}^{t_n}\int_K f$. The backward-Euler step seeks $u^n$ with zero boundary face values satisfying
$$ \sum_{K\in\mathcal K}|K|\frac{u_K^n-u_K^{n-1}}{t_n-t_{n-1}}v_K+\sum_{K\in\mathcal K}\mathcal A_{h,K}(u^n;v)=\sum_{K\in\mathcal K}|K|f_K^n v_K $$
for every test vector with zero boundary face values. The formula specifies a candidate discrete method; solvability and convergence require separate results.

For an affine function $\ell(x)=b\cdot x+c$, its cell and face averages satisfy $G_K\ell=b$ and $\rho_{K,F}(\ell)=0$ by the displayed face-moment closure. The drawing illustrates the cell and face degrees of freedom on a skew cell; no center-to-face orthogonality is assumed.

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=1]
  \draw[thick] (0,0) -- (2,0) -- (3,1) -- (1,1) -- cycle;
  \fill (1.5,0.5) circle (2pt) node[below] {$u_K$};
  \fill (1,0) circle (2pt) node[below] {$u_{F_1}$};
  \fill (2.5,0.5) circle (2pt) node[right] {$u_{F_2}$};
  \fill (2,1) circle (2pt) node[above] {$u_{F_3}$};
  \fill (0.5,0.5) circle (2pt) node[left] {$u_{F_4}$};
  \draw[->,blue] (1.5,0.5) -- (2.2,0.5) node[right] {$G_Ku$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

When $p=2$, $b_K(\xi)=A_K\xi$, and $\alpha_{0,K}=\lambda_{\min}(A_K)$, the nonlinear formula agrees with the linear form above. Neither specification by itself proves solvability, a conforming $W_0^{1,p}$ reconstruction, or a mesh-uniform discrete Aubin–Lions estimate; those require separate results or hypotheses.

Let a finite boundary-anchored cell-face mesh satisfy the face-moment closure in [[def-hybrid-mimetic-fv-scheme]], and let every $A_K$ be symmetric positive definite. Define
$$ \|v\|_{K,\mathrm{mim}}^2=|K||G_Kv|^2+\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\frac{|F|}{d_{K,F}}\rho_{K,F}(v)^2. $$
Then $\mathscr A_K(v,v)\ge\lambda_{\min}(A_K)\|v\|_{K,\mathrm{mim}}^2$. The global Dirichlet matrix of the linear hybrid mimetic scheme is symmetric positive definite and has a unique solution for every finite cell-source vector. Its induced numerical fluxes satisfy the cellwise balance and opposite-flux identity on each interior face. For any affine $\ell(x)=b\cdot x+c$, the local linear flux is exactly $Q_{K,F}(\ell)=-|F|(A_Kb)\cdot n_{K,F}$. For the nonlinear $p$-growth extension in [[def-hybrid-mimetic-fv-scheme]], the spatial operator is monotone and coercive in the reconstructed gradient and residual variables, and its shared interior face fluxes are conservative at each implicit time step.

The cell and face means of $u$ are $u_K=5/2$ and $(u_F)=(1,7/2,4,3/2)$. Substitution into [F1] gives $\sum_F|F|u_Fn_{K,F}=(2,4)$ and hence $G_Ku=(1,2)=\nabla u$. We have $A\nabla u=(2,2)$. By [F2], the outward integrated fluxes in bottom/right/top/left order are $4,0,-4,0$, respectively. Their sum is zero, which is the exact cell balance for the affine state since its flux is constant and has zero divergence. This verifies affine consistency and local conservation on this skew, anisotropic cell.
